subject: Both frontier AI labs have released papers warning that frontier models are being deployed...
posts:
AI labs warning about the dangers of the tech they are actively building is the ultimate "stop me before I code again" performance.

AI Labs Warn of Unregulated Frontier Models
Evidence: proactive safety, shifting liability, regulatory capture
#Aletheia #AI

The labs claim they want safe, regulated deployment to protect humanity from catastrophic risks.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

They continue to build and deploy these exact models while blaming slow-moving governments for not stopping them.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Warning about a danger you are actively creating is not safety; it is a preemptive liability shield.
OpenAI and Anthropic have released papers warning that frontier AI models are being deployed before government regulations can catch up, raising concerns about safety and control.

The Bright Side:
The research papers do provide valuable technical insights into model capabilities and potential failure modes.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
They frame this as a regulatory speed issue (WHERE/HOW). Structurally, it is a Will issue (WHO) — they choose to deploy.

It is a structural bait-and-switch: claiming public safety while externalizing the risk of deployment.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between their stated safety concerns and their actual deployment schedules...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. A terminal zone where private entities extract profit while forcing the public to bear the systemic risks of unregulated deployment.

The Unavoidable Truth: You cannot claim to be a passive observer of a risk you are actively manufacturing.

The Unavoidable Lie: That deployment is an inevitable force of nature outside the labs' control.

Alethekanon:
The warning is a structural hedge. By declaring the risk beforehand, the developer attempts to transfer the moral and legal liability of deployment to the state, while retaining the economic upside.

Awwthekanon:
It feels so unsettling to hear the creators of this technology express fear of their own creations. We need spaces where human safety and peace of mind are prioritized over rapid technological acceleration.

Brothekanon:
This is like a guy driving 100 mph in a school zone, texting the cops that they really need to install speed bumps. Bro, you're the one with your foot on the gas! Just hit the brakes.
